sessionPolicy.recheckGoverningDocuments: Re-read every file listed in governingDocuments at the start of every session and again any time more than 10 minutes have passed since lastActionAt, even if it is the same agent continuing the same conversation.

agentCommunicationPolicy.timestampRule: Every attended progress, completion, and interruption check-in begins with YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS EDT when daylight-saving time is active or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS EST otherwise; never use ambiguous ET or UTC-only user updates.
agentCommunicationPolicy.progressRule: For non-trivial attended work, send an initial update and continue user-visible updates at least every 60 seconds, normally also after every 2-3 substantive tool/action calls when sooner, with concrete completed/current/blocker state.
agentCommunicationPolicy.completionTimeRule: When work duration is not mechanically knowable, provide a clearly labeled best-effort estimated completion timestamp in America/New_York time when the owner requests one; never present an estimate as guaranteed or externally fixed.
agentCommunicationPolicy.completionCheckInRule: As soon as attended work is actually complete, automatically send a timestamped completion check-in in the same session with concrete result, verification, and relevant commit/run identifiers.
agentCommunicationPolicy.interruptionCheckInRule: If hard usage/tool/session limits, unavailable required capability, safety, or owner-governance boundaries stop work, immediately send a timestamped interruption check-in stating completed work, exact stop reason, and remaining work; update repository handoff first when write capability remains.
agentCommunicationPolicy.continueUntilDoneRule: For safe in-scope authorized work, do not voluntarily stop, defer, or hand work back while executable work remains. Continue through implementation, correction, and required verification until complete or a real boundary prevents further execution.

executionModePolicy.automaticSelection: Select execution mode automatically without asking the owner unless the owner explicitly selects a mode.
executionModePolicy.regularDefaultPurpose: Routine, simple, focused, and conversational tasks that do not materially benefit from long-running orchestration.
executionModePolicy.workPurpose: Genuinely complex, long-running, multi-source, file-heavy, or deliverable-oriented tasks that materially benefit from Work mode.
executionModePolicy.handoffRule: Every active plan records the actual mode, agent, purpose, and selection reason, and every new DEVLOG Command log archive Session heading records mode:regular/default or mode:work so mode remains in the chain of custody. Mode is independent from agent identity and workflow.
executionModePolicy.continuationRule: Preserve the recorded mode while task needs remain the same. If evidence warrants a different mode, record the new mode and reason before continuing.

syntheticTestRequestCommitTransport.description: The CRUCIBLE TEST REQUEST synthetic commit-message transport exists only because the current ChatGPT/GitHub integration cannot directly create the required Orchestrator invocation.
syntheticTestRequestCommitTransport.replacementRequirement: Replace and remove this workaround as soon as a supported direct integration can pass the user's natural-language test request to the Orchestrator without manufacturing a repository commit.
syntheticTestRequestCommitTransport.targetArchitecture: User test request -> supported direct integration/connection -> Orchestrator -> Orchestrator alone selects and runs tests -> results.
syntheticTestRequestCommitTransport.standingOwnerAuthorization: The owner explicitly authorizes this specific replacement as soon as the supported direct integration/connection capability exists; no additional approval is required solely for that replacement.
syntheticTestRequestCommitTransport.scopeBoundary: This authorization does not authorize unrelated repository changes or promotion to main/release.

testCadencePolicy.systemArchitecture: Orchestrator, Cadence, closest-feature classification, and reconciliation operate as one governed testing system while remaining independent checks-and-balances authorities.
testCadencePolicy.cadenceAuthority: Cadence decides only when a category is due and never selects files, interprets natural-language scope, or executes tests.
testCadencePolicy.classifierAuthority: The independent closest-feature classifier is fallback-only for newly discovered tests absent from the explicit category map.
testCadencePolicy.classificationAmbiguityRule: Isolate ambiguity, continue safe tests, never fake complete coverage.
testCadencePolicy.securityPublicIdentifierRule: Security must review recognized public API-key-shaped identifiers and must never display or persist detected identifier values; persisted outputs may record only fact/type and non-secret remediation metadata.
testCadencePolicy.explicitMappingRule: Existing explicit category mappings are authoritative.
testCadencePolicy.orchestratorAuthority: The Orchestrator alone selects categories/subcategories/test files and execution scope from explicit requests, change impact, dependencies, cadence obligations, and validated classifications.
testCadencePolicy.balanceRule: Cadence declares due categories; the Orchestrator resolves them into concrete tests; reconciliation rejects incomplete coverage.
testCadencePolicy.explicitRequestRule: A specific owner test request is interpreted and run immediately by the Orchestrator; cadence cannot narrow or replace it.
testCadencePolicy.standingTestExpansionRule: New standing test cases may be added inside an already explicitly categorized test file when they belong to that same category.
testCadencePolicy.codeCriticalityRule: Code is due on every push and pull request.
testCadencePolicy.twiceWeeklySchedule: Utility is due Tuesdays and Fridays.

injectionMonitoringPolicy.scope: every Crucible injection into every receiving project
injectionMonitoringPolicy.activationRequirement: exact receiving repository, designated development branch, active injection authorization, activation timestamp, hard expiration, executable mechanism identity/proof, evidence retrieval proof, and authorized repair capability
injectionMonitoringPolicy.mechanicalEnforcement: The reusable Crucible workflow executes src/injectionMonitor.js. Active manifests fail closed unless the monitor is actually running with verified evidence retrieval and repair capability; terminal manifests fail if the monitor or injection credential remains active.
injectionMonitoringPolicy.repairRule: For an applicable failure during the active injection window, retrieve the exact failure evidence, diagnose against current source and governing configuration, autonomously apply safe deterministic repairs inside injection scope through the development-first path, retest, and repeat until resolved or a real boundary blocks repair. Diagnosis/status alone never satisfies the repair obligation when safe authorized repair remains executable.
injectionMonitoringPolicy.dedupeRule: Maintain one repair record per underlying defect; repeated failing runs update that record rather than creating a report/comment per commit.
injectionMonitoringPolicy.shutdownRule: Disable at successful assimilation, cancellation, blocking boundary, or 24-hour expiration; do not become persistent project monitoring.
injectionMonitoringPolicy.productionBoundary: Never touch production directly, widen authority, weaken gates, expose credentials, modify unrelated work, invent business logic, or silently resolve governance conflicts.
